study.title: PHA / HAZOP – Ammonia unit: reforming, fuel gas, synthesis, refrigeration and purge recovery (worked example)
study.project: PHA of the ammonia unit – selected nodes for training
study.scope: Five of the 27 nodes of the ammonia unit: N01 (source node 3) desulfurised feed gas with steam through the mixed-feed preheat coil to the primary reformer 101-B and the secondary reformer 103-D; N02 (source node 23) fuel gas to the primary-reformer arch burners 101-BBA, tunnel burners 101-BBT and superheater burners 101-BBS; N03 (source node 15) synthesis gas compressor 103-J and ammonia converter 105-D; N04 (source node 17) ammonia refrigeration – compressor 105-J, unitized chiller 120-C with flash drums 120-CF1…CF4, condenser 127-C and receiver 149-D; N05 (source node 18) loop purge-gas ammonia recovery with the ammonia distillation column 160-C.
study.exclusions: The other 22 nodes of the source study (front-end, CO shift, CO2 removal, methanator, steam, drains); ammonia storage tanks; urea plant. Licensor proprietary design details.
study.basis: Reform natural gas with steam (steam-to-carbon ratio 3.0) at about 33 barg and 800 °C, make synthesis gas, compress it to about 140 barg and convert it to ammonia in 105-D; condense and refrigerate the product with an ammonia refrigeration system (flash drums 120-CF1/CF2 designed for 15.5 barg and 0.25 bar vacuum – source 15.8 kg/cm2G); recover ammonia from the loop purge. All values are illustrative.
study.modes: Normal operation, start-up (start-up heater 102-B, catalyst reduction), shutdown and depressurisation, compressor trip and restart, maintenance isolation

sessions.notes: Node 3 (primary and secondary reforming) – source worksheet reviewed and risk-ranked; tube rupture and steam-to-carbon trips.
Node 23 (reformer fuel gas and BMS) – firebox explosion and light-off.
Node 15 (syngas compressor and converter) – converter over-temperature referred to FT-AM-02 and BT-AM-02; releases to ETA-AM-02.
Node 17 (refrigeration) – receiver overpressure referred to FT-AM-01; ammonia release to FT-AM-03, ETA-AM-01 and BT-AM-01.
Node 18 (purge-gas recovery) – gas blow-by into 160-C. Study closed; FMECA on 23–24 Nov.

nodes.name: Source node 3 – Feed gas and steam to the primary reformer 101-B and secondary reformer 103-D
nodes.batteryLimits: From the desulfurizer outlet via feed control FV-1001 (FIC-1001), steam addition (FIC-1002 / FV-1002, ratio FFI-1001) and the mixed-feed preheat coil 101-BCA1 to the catalyst tubes of 101-B, and with process air to the secondary reformer 103-D; trips XV-1201 (feed) on FFSLL-1201 low steam-to-carbon and FSLL-1201 low steam
nodes.description: Reform desulfurised natural gas with steam over nickel catalyst at a steam-to-carbon ratio of 3.0, and complete the reforming with process air in 103-D
nodes.designParams: 101-B tubes: design 800 °C metal / 41 barg; TAH-1325 tube outlet; FFSLL-1201 trips at steam-to-carbon 2.5; PSHH-1059 high pressure
nodes.operatingParams: Inlet 38 barg, outlet 33 barg; reformer outlet 800 °C; 103-D outlet 1 000 °C
nodes.materials: Natural gas, steam, synthesis gas (H2, CO – flammable, toxic CO), process air

nodes.name: Source node 23 – Fuel gas to the primary reformer arch burners 101-BBA, tunnel burners 101-BBT and superheater burners 101-BBS
nodes.batteryLimits: From fuel-gas pressure control PIC-1001B / PV-1001B and PV-1002B through the double block-and-bleed shut-off valves XV-1220A/C and XV-1222A/C (arch), XV-1240A/C (tunnel) and XV-1245A/C (superheater) to the burners; BMS with flame scanners BSLL-1200 / BSLL-1201, PSLL-1221 / PSHH-1221 and PAHH-1226 (firebox pressure)
nodes.description: Deliver fuel gas to the reformer burners only when the furnace is purged, combustion air is proven and flames are proven, and shut it off on any unsafe condition
nodes.designParams: Fuel gas header 6 barg design; PSLL-1221 0.3 barg; PSHH-1221 2.5 barg; firebox pressure trip PAHH-1226 (loss of draught)
nodes.operatingParams: Burner pressure 0.5–2.0 barg; firebox −5 mmWC; about 400 burners
nodes.materials: Natural gas fuel, purge gas from N05 (H2-rich), flue gas (CO)

nodes.name: Source node 15 – Synthesis gas compressor 103-J and ammonia converter 105-D
nodes.batteryLimits: From the syngas compressor suction (PSLL-1155) through 103-J (steam turbine 103-JT, anti-surge FV-1008 / FIC-1008) to the synthesis loop, start-up heater 102-B, converter 105-D with bed temperatures TAH-1383 / TSHH-1396, and the loop exchangers 123-C1 and 124-C1 to the chiller 120-C
nodes.description: Compress synthesis gas to about 140 barg and convert hydrogen and nitrogen to ammonia over iron catalyst at 380–520 °C without exceeding the loop design
nodes.designParams: Loop design 160 barg / 400 °C (converter shell); converter catalyst 520 °C max; TSHH-1396 trips 103-J and closes the converter feed; PSV-1018 on the loop at 155 barg
nodes.operatingParams: Loop 135–145 barg; converter outlet 450 °C; 103-J speed 10 000 rpm
nodes.materials: Synthesis gas (75 % H2 – extremely flammable, high-temperature hydrogen attack), ammonia (toxic)

nodes.name: Source node 17 – Ammonia refrigeration: 105-J, unitized chiller 120-C, flash drums 120-CF1…CF4, condenser 127-C, receiver 149-D
nodes.batteryLimits: From the flash drums 120-CF1/CF2/CF3/CF4 (levels LIC-1015A, LSHH-1214…1217) through the stages of refrigeration compressor 105-J (anti-surge FV-1009…1012) to condenser 127-C and receiver 149-D (PIC-1009, PAH-1009, PAH-1109), and the boil-off from storage via XV-1801
nodes.description: Refrigerate the synthesis loop and condense product ammonia, keeping the flash drums within their pressure and level limits and liquid out of 105-J
nodes.designParams: Flash drums 120-CF1/CF2 design 15.5 barg and 0.25 bar vacuum (source 15.8 kg/cm2G); receiver 149-D 20 barg, PSV-1109 at 20 barg; LSHH-1214…1217 trip 105-J; PSHH-1110 high discharge pressure trip; design minimum temperature −33 °C
nodes.operatingParams: Flash drums −33 to +10 °C; condenser 127-C 16–18 barg; about 4 000 t refrigerant inventory hold-up 120 t
nodes.materials: Liquid and vapour ammonia (toxic, IDLH 300 ppm, corrosive; flammable 15–28 %)

nodes.name: Source node 18 – Loop purge-gas ammonia recovery and ammonia distillation column 160-C
nodes.batteryLimits: From the loop purge (FIC-1027 / FV-1027) through the purge-gas scrubber 124-D (wash water FV-1029) and the ammonia distillation column 160-C (PIC-1033, LIC-1049, reboiler 161-C1, reflux pumps 161-J) to the recovered-ammonia return and the purge gas to the reformer fuel (N02)
nodes.description: Recover ammonia from the loop purge so that the purge gas sent to fuel is ammonia-free, and return the ammonia to the product
nodes.designParams: Scrubber 124-D 160 barg; column 160-C 20 barg, PSV-1033 at 20 barg; FAL-1064 low wash-water flow
nodes.operatingParams: Purge 140 barg reduced to 20 barg; column 18 barg
nodes.materials: Ammonia (toxic), purge gas (H2, CH4, Ar – flammable), aqueous ammonia

deviations.deviation: No / low steam flow to the reformer feed
deviations.consequence: Steam-to-carbon ratio falls; carbon deposits on the reformer catalyst and tubes overheat – tube rupture, fire in the 101-B firebox

deviations.deviation: High feed gas flow
deviations.consequence: Low steam-to-carbon ratio (as N01-01) and under-reforming; higher methane slip downstream

deviations.deviation: Reverse flow of process gas into the steam header
deviations.consequence: Process gas (H2, CO) into the steam system – flammable and toxic gas in the steam header and at steam users

deviations.deviation: High reformer tube temperature
deviations.consequence: Tube creep and rupture; release of syngas into the firebox – fire, possible firebox overpressure

deviations.deviation: High reformer inlet pressure
deviations.consequence: Reformer tubes and the mixed-feed coil above design

deviations.deviation: High process-air flow to the secondary reformer 103-D
deviations.consequence: Over-temperature in 103-D (combustion zone) – refractory and shell damage; hot spots on the 103-D shell

deviations.deviation: Sulphur slip from the desulfurizer
deviations.consequence: Poisoning of the reformer catalyst – tube hot bands, reduced conversion

deviations.deviation: Loss of instrument air or power
deviations.consequence: Feed valves fail closed (fail-safe), reformer trips; uncontrolled restart risks low steam-to-carbon

deviations.deviation: Start-up – steam before feed sequence
deviations.consequence: Carbon formation and tube overheating at start-up

deviations.deviation: Loss of fuel gas – burner flame-out
deviations.consequence: Burners go out; if gas returns with the valves open, unburnt gas accumulates in the 101-B firebox – explosion on relight
deviations.lopaNotes: L-07: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 (Safety, RRF 10); with proposed IPLs: Meets target – accepted IPLs only; L-08: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 (Safety, RRF 10); with proposed IPLs: Meets target – accepted IPLs only; L-09: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 (Safety, RRF 5); with proposed IPLs: Meets target – accepted IPLs only

deviations.deviation: High fuel-gas pressure at the burners
deviations.consequence: Over-firing, flame lift-off and flame-out with gas flowing – firebox explosion; tube overheating

deviations.deviation: Low fuel-gas pressure
deviations.consequence: Flame instability, flame-out

deviations.deviation: Ammonia or liquids in the fuel gas
deviations.consequence: NOx emissions, burner fouling and flame instability; liquid can extinguish burners

deviations.deviation: Loss of induced draught (ID fan trip)
deviations.consequence: Firebox goes to positive pressure – flames and flue gas out of the peep holes; burns to operators

deviations.deviation: Light-off without adequate purge
deviations.consequence: Explosive mixture in the firebox at light-off – firebox explosion

deviations.deviation: High liquid level in the fuel-gas knock-out drum
deviations.consequence: Liquid carry-over to the burners (as N02-04)

deviations.deviation: Fuel-gas leak at the burner manifold
deviations.consequence: Gas fire on the burner platform; operator burns

deviations.deviation: No flow – 103-J trips
deviations.consequence: Loop circulation stops; converter 105-D heats up if the start-up heater 102-B is firing; plant shutdown

deviations.deviation: Low suction flow – compressor surge
deviations.consequence: Surge – thrust-bearing and seal damage, possible seal failure and hydrogen release at 103-J

deviations.deviation: Converter catalyst over-temperature
deviations.consequence: Catalyst damage; converter shell and outlet exchanger above design temperature – flange leak or rupture, high-temperature hydrogen attack; syngas fire
deviations.comments: Quantified in fault tree FT-AM-02 (top 1.8E-2 /yr); threat T1 of bow tie BT-AM-02. Likelihood after safeguards from the calculated frequency 1.8E-2 /yr.
deviations.lopaNotes: L-04: SIL 2 needed (Safety, RRF 102); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only; L-05: SIL 2 needed (Safety, RRF 205); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only; L-06: SIL 1 needed (Safety, RRF 51.1); with proposed IPLs: Meets target – accepted IPLs only

deviations.deviation: High synthesis loop pressure
deviations.consequence: Loop above design (160 barg) – flange failure, large syngas release

deviations.deviation: High inerts / wrong H2:N2 ratio
deviations.consequence: Loop pressure rises; conversion drops; temperature excursions in 105-D

deviations.deviation: High-temperature hydrogen attack of loop exchangers
deviations.consequence: Sudden failure of 123-C1 / 124-C1 – syngas jet fire

deviations.deviation: Reverse rotation / back-flow on compressor trip
deviations.consequence: Compressor reverse rotation – seal and bearing damage, gas release at the seals

deviations.deviation: Syngas leak at the compressor or loop flanges
deviations.consequence: Hydrogen-rich jet fire; vapour cloud explosion in the congested compressor house
deviations.lopaNotes: L-10: SIL 1 needed (Safety, RRF 70); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only; L-11: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 (Safety, RRF 7); with proposed IPLs: Meets target – accepted IPLs only

deviations.deviation: Start-up heater 102-B firing without loop circulation
deviations.consequence: Converter overheating at start-up

deviations.deviation: High pressure in the refrigerant condenser 127-C and receiver 149-D
deviations.consequence: Refrigerant system above design; PSV-1109 lifts to the flare; if relief fails – rupture and large liquid ammonia release (toxic cloud)
deviations.comments: Quantified in fault tree FT-AM-01 (top 2.4E-6 /yr); threat T1 of bow tie BT-AM-01. Likelihood after safeguards from the calculated frequency 2.4E-6 /yr.
deviations.lopaNotes: L-01: SIL 1 needed (Community, RRF 10.2); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only; L-02: SIL 1 needed (Community, RRF 10.2); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only; L-03: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 (Community, RRF 2.05); with proposed IPLs: Meets target – accepted IPLs only

deviations.deviation: High level in a flash drum 120-CF1…CF4
deviations.consequence: Liquid ammonia carried into the 105-J suction – compressor damage, seal failure and ammonia release

deviations.deviation: Low pressure / vacuum in flash drums 120-CF1 / 120-CF2
deviations.consequence: Loss of suction to the 105-J stages – compressor damage; vacuum in the flash drums (designed for 0.25 bar vacuum)

deviations.deviation: Choking of the 105-J suction strainers
deviations.consequence: Loss of suction to a stage of 105-J – surge and compressor damage

deviations.deviation: Low temperature – auto-refrigeration on depressurisation
deviations.consequence: Brittle fracture of carbon steel below −33 °C – sudden ammonia release

deviations.deviation: Loss of cooling water
deviations.consequence: Condenser 127-C pressure rises (as N04-01)

deviations.deviation: Ammonia leak from the refrigerant pumps, flanges or receiver
deviations.consequence: Toxic ammonia cloud in the refrigeration area; exposure of operators and, for large releases, people off site

deviations.deviation: Line break on ammonia service
deviations.consequence: Ammonia spray onto the maintenance crew – chemical burns, inhalation

deviations.deviation: Relief discharge of ammonia to the flare
deviations.consequence: Ammonia to the flare – NOx; if the flare is out, toxic ammonia release at height

deviations.deviation: No wash-water flow to the purge-gas scrubber 124-D
deviations.consequence: Ammonia slips into the purge gas to fuel (N02) – NOx and burner problems; ammonia odour around the reformer

deviations.deviation: High pressure in the distillation column 160-C
deviations.consequence: Column (20 barg design) over-pressured – rupture and ammonia release

deviations.deviation: High level in column 160-C
deviations.consequence: Liquid ammonia carry-over into the purge gas to fuel

deviations.deviation: Low level in the purge-gas scrubber 124-D
deviations.consequence: Gas blow-by from 140 barg into the low-pressure ammonia return (as N05-02)

deviations.deviation: High column bottoms temperature
deviations.consequence: Column pressure rises; water carry-over into the recovered ammonia

deviations.deviation: Ammonia leak at the column pumps 161-J
deviations.consequence: Toxic ammonia release at the recovery unit

deviations.deviation: Power failure
deviations.consequence: Pumps stop, column pressure falls; purge flow to fuel stops – reformer fuel balance upset

causes.text: Steam supply failure (boiler trip, FV-1002 closes)
Steam pressure lower than reformer pressure (steam trip)
Feed introduced before steam flow is established
Liquid slug in the fuel gas
Purge gas from N05 at high pressure
Ammonia carry-over in purge gas from N05
Fuel valves passing into the cold firebox
Flange / flexible hose failure at a burner
Discharge check valve fails to close
Flange leak on hot hydrogen service
Loss of boil-off from storage – XV-1801 closes
Rapid depressurisation of a liquid-full section
Ammonia flashing through a passing valve
Purge let-down PV-1033A fails open – gas blow-by from 140 barg

recs.text: Confirm that the low steam-to-carbon trip FFSLL-1201 and the low steam trip FSLL-1201 are independent of the ratio controller FFI-1001 (separate transmitters) and SIL-assessed.
Install tube-wall temperature monitoring (fixed IR scanners) on the primary reformer 101-B and add tube-wall limits to the operating window.
Review the process-air trip FFSHH-1203 response time against the secondary reformer 103-D over-temperature scenario.
Verify the reformer BMS flame-failure function against IEC 61511 (scanners per burner row, proof-test interval) – the arch burners 101-BBA run at low turndown during start-up.
Route the purge gas from N05 to the reformer fuel only through the knock-out drum with an ammonia analyser and automatic diversion to the flare on high ammonia.
Provide differential-pressure indication across the suction strainers of 103-J and 105-J (source recommendation 89).
Consult the compressor vendor on the response to suction-strainer choking leading to low suction pressure (source recommendation 104).

Upgrade the converter over-temperature protection: fault tree FT-AM-02 gives an uncontrolled over-temperature frequency of 1.8E-2 /yr with protection PFDavg 5.1E-2; add a second independent bed thermocouple to TSHH-1396 (1oo2) and a six-monthly trip test.
Confirm the loop relief PSV-1018 is sized for the start-up heater 102-B fire case and for blocked outlet with 103-J at maximum speed.
Carry out a high-temperature hydrogen attack (HTHA) review of the loop exchangers 123-C1 / 124-C1 against the current Nelson curves.

Refrigeration overpressure: fault tree FT-AM-01 gives 2.4E-6 /yr with protection PFDavg 1.1E-5, but almost all of the credit is PSV-1109 – every demand ends as an ammonia relief to flare because the alarm and the trip share one transmitter; make PSHH-1110 independent of PIC-1009 and add an automatic start of the standby cooling-water pump.
Verify the ammonia detection and ESD (FT-AM-03 PFDavg 2.9E-2): detectors at the receiver 149-D, the refrigerant pumps and the compressor house, 1oo3 with automatic isolation of XV-1290.
Extend the water-spray curtain to the refrigerant pump bay and test it annually; event tree ETA-AM-01 gives 1.3E-6 /yr for off-site toxic impact.
Confirm all refrigeration piping and the flash drums are rated for −33 °C including depressurisation (auto-refrigeration of ammonia).
Add a low-low cooling-water flow trip at condenser 127-C that unloads 105-J before PSV-1109 lifts.
Provide a toxic-gas refuge procedure and annual drill for the ammonia area; confirm HVAC trip on ammonia at the control room.
Add high-level protection LAH-1049 / LSHH on column 160-C to prevent liquid ammonia carry-over into the purge gas to fuel.
Confirm that the purge let-down PV-1033A fail-open (gas blow-by) case is covered by PSV-1033 (160 barg into a 20 barg column).
Syngas release outcomes: event tree ETA-AM-02 gives 8.1E-5 /yr for a vapour cloud explosion at the synthesis loop; review congestion and the remote depressurisation HV-1019 response time.
Add a start-up permissive: 102-B start-up heater may only fire with proven loop circulation (103-J running) – overheating of the converter at start-up.
